reuse.why: Extends the existing WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule and reuses recurConfigToRSchedule, but rewrites applyWeekendRule's body so the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend is left unused, and the new handler re-derives the daily-skip rule instead of calling a shared one.

duplication.why: The daily-skip decision (skipWeekend && daily && (isWeekend || isHoliday)) is written once in getNextDate and again in getDatesInRange, and the weekend-moving logic now exists both in the orphaned getDateWithSkippedWeekend and in the new applyWeekendRule loop.

placement.why: Holiday matching and the weekend rule stay in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in schedules/app.ts, but the daily-skip rule is embedded in getNextDate and the handler rather than in the weekend-rule layer.

scope.why: Mostly focused, with a gratuitous import reorder in schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: Daily handling is special-cased in two places with a magic take count (holidays.length + 8) in getNextDate, the safety throw for an unknown solve mode was dropped, and a dead helper remains, so the rule is easy to change inconsistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: applyWeekendRule no longer goes through getDateWithSkippedWeekend (shared/schedules.ts), and getDatesInRange (schedules/app.ts) applies its own daily-skip check before applyWeekendRule instead of a shared rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily weekend/holiday skip appears as a find() over extra occurrences in getNextDate and as a map-to-null filter in getDatesInRange; the weekend move is reshaped as an addDays loop in applyWeekendRule while getDateWithSkippedWeekend still holds the old version.

abstraction_drift.where: holidays added to WeekendRule; getNextDate gains a daily-only take count and a daily-only skip branch; getDatesInRange re-implements the daily skip instead of using a shared definition.
